page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7nex.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps. The underlying Intel Xeon architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX, AVX-512F, AVX512_VNNI, AES, and SHA_NI, which accelerate cryptographic and vector-based calculations.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates moderate single-core capabilities but exhibits limitations under multi-threaded workloads. Single-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests place the processor in the average performance tier, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also achieve average marks. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by lower scores in multi-threaded stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both small and large blocks fall into the lower performance brackets, though Passmark memory tests and static web serving throughput maintain average ratings.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c7nex.xlarge offers a dedicated hardware profile tailored for workloads that require predictable CPU allocation without the overhead of hyperthreading. Because it lacks local storage and has a low memory-to-vCPU ratio, it is best suited for compute-bound tasks that do not demand massive memory footprints or high-speed local disk I/O. Tradeoffs include weaker multi-core scaling and lower memory bandwidth, which may affect highly parallelized operations.

This instance is appropriate for workloads such as lightweight web serving, single-threaded batch processing, basic cryptography tasks, and utility applications that benefit from dedicated CPU resources but do not require extensive memory or local storage.
